title: Cut slowest athena-cli test binaries' run time without weakening tests
summary: Retry of the test-suite speedup, following the user's reply: nextest is rejected (584 s vs 673 s, about 13%), so the job instead finds where lifecycle, job_plan, drain, retry and steward tests spend time and cuts it. Audience: the user, who reads docs/decisions.md and later job times.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria require measured before/after times and a passing full suite, not just edited files.
Decision numbers must be measured in the job or labeled as brain-measured or estimates.
cargo test, clippy and fmt must be clean.
Limited to the test timing change, with no tool or CI changes.
Behavior criteria use cargo commands the verifier can run.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The user's latest reply (do not adopt nextest; speed up the slowest binaries; target full cargo test under 6 minutes) overrides the earlier nextest readings.
Test paths are inferred from the user's binary names; the producer finds the real files and shared helpers.
The 6-minute target is measured by the producer on its own machine and reported; the verifier can only confirm tests pass.
Request priority is high and speed first, but this is not marked urgent since it only asks for a speedup.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/decisions.md has a new decision with per-binary before and after times (measured in the job, labeled as measured) for athena-cli tests/lifecycle.rs, job_plan.rs, drain.rs, retry.rs and steward.rs, and the cause found for each (sleeps, poll intervals, repeated setup, locks, or real git/process work).

The decision records the compile 67 s versus run 673 s split (4 cores, measured by the brain) and lists cargo-nextest 0.9.148 (584 s vs 673 s, about 13%) as a rejected alternative with that reason; it also lists sccache per D79 and a shared target dir as considered alternatives, and claims no unmeasured number.

No test is deleted, ignored, or has its assertions weakened; the test count under cargo test --locked is not lower than before, and no athena.toml, ci.yml or tool pin is changed. CHANGELOG.md has an entry.

Speedups come from test-only mechanisms such as shorter test intervals, fixtures built once, or avoiding needless git/process work, and production defaults are unchanged unless a test-only override is added.
Run `cargo test --locked`: it passes with every test still running, and the job's reported wall time is under 6 minutes on its machine. A test that fails still fails the run.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`: both clean.

out_of_scope: Adopting cargo-nextest or any new pinned tool
Changing athena.toml, ci.yml, or the test check
Removing, ignoring, or weakening any test
Adopting sccache or a shared target directory
departures: Producer must time several slow test binaries (about 11 minutes per full run), so cost and time exceed the reference.
urgent_reason: Speeding up the suite cuts check and producer minutes on every later job, which is wasted time.
